contamination.brief_line: 注意：以下摘录的锚点未通过逐字核对，已删除；简报中引用它们的句子也已删除，不得写入相关内容：SJ0651-E9。

issues.problem: “守边多年”/“for years”的时间跨度在证据中没有依据。证据只记载他被任命为西河守。

evidence.quote: 乃以為西河守，以拒秦、韓

issues.proposed: 改为“在魏国任西河守、功劳明确的吴起”/“He had held Wei's western frontier at Xihe”
issues.rationale: 删去证据无据的“守边多年/for years”，改为“在魏国任西河守”，英文同步改为 held Wei's western frontier at Xihe。

issues.problem: “位置稳固”/“his footing looked secure”无证据支持。证据中他与田文争位且不悦，并不能说明稳固。
issues.proposed: 删去“位置稳固”/“and his footing looked secure”
issues.rationale: 中文删去“位置稳固”，英文删去 and his footing looked secure；同时去掉正文中的证据编号。

issues.problem: 英文“gone south to the state of Chu”中的方位“south”证据没有记载，中文也没有对应内容。
issues.proposed: 改为“had gone to the state of Chu”
issues.rationale: 英文删去证据未载的方位 south，改为 had gone to the state of Chu。

issues.problem: 中文用「」标出的「留不留心」「拒绝」都不是证据中的逐字片段。
issues.proposed: 改用引号“”或不加引号；如要引原文，可用「起有留心則必受之」
issues.rationale: 中文“留不留心”“拒绝”不是原文逐字片段，改用“”。

issues.problem: 英文多出中文没有的“a matter that takes an hour to justify”；中文末尾有（作者解释）标注，英文前两句没有解释标签。
issues.proposed: 英文改为“cannot easily turn his refusal into a large matter to be explained”，并在段首加“One reading is that…”或注明为作者解释
issues.rationale: 英文删去中文没有的 takes an hour to justify，改为 cannot easily turn his refusal into a large matter to be explained；段首加 In the author's reading，与中文的（作者解释）对应。

issues.problem: 英文把“衛”译作“Wei”，与下文的魏国（Wei）同名，读者会把吴起的母国误读为魏国，事实因此混淆。
issues.proposed: 衛统一译作“Wey”（或加注“Wei 衛, not the later Wei 魏”）
issues.rationale: 英文把衛改译为 Wey，并注明它与吴起后来效力的魏国不同，避免误读。

issues.problem: 英文“Wei's capital”“Lu and Wei are brother states”同样把衛与魏混用；“to slight Wei”把“棄衛”（抛弃卫国）弱化了，与中文“抛弃卫国”不一致。
issues.proposed: 衛改译“Wey”；“slight Wei”改为“abandon Wey”
issues.rationale: 英文的衛统一译作 Wey；to slight Wei 改为 to abandon Wey，与中文“抛弃卫国”一致。

issues.problem: “摔门离开卫国”没有依据。原文只说从卫国郭门向东出走，没有摔门这一动作。英文“walked out through the eastern gate”基本相符，中英也因此不一致。
issues.proposed: 改为“从卫国郭门向东出走”
issues.rationale: 中文“摔门离开卫国”改为“从卫国郭门向东出走”；英文同步改为 went out eastward through the outer gate of Wey's city wall。

issues.problem: “鲁君起疑，辞退了吴起”/“grew suspicious and dismissed him”在证据中无记载。证据只有进言内容，没有鲁君的反应或罢免。context.2“这套说法之所以有效”也建立在这一虚构结果上。
issues.proposed: 删去该句，或改为“证据包未记载鲁君听后的处置”；context.2相应删去“之所以有效”的前提
issues.rationale: 删去证据无载的“鲁君起疑，辞退了吴起”，改为说明所据原文止于这段进言、未记鲁君的处置。context.2 的“之所以有效”改为“这套说法的着力点”，不再以虚构结果为前提；英文同步加 The author infers 标签。

issues.problem: 誓言原文为“不為卿相”。中文作“不做上卿”，英文作“highest office”，都与原文不符。
issues.proposed: 改为“不做卿相不回卫国”/“until he became a minister or chancellor”
issues.rationale: 誓言中文改为“不做卿相不回卫国”，英文改为 until he became a high minister or chancellor，与原文一致。

issues.problem: 「人」「账」用了「」，但不是证据引语，违反「」只用于逐字引文的规则。
issues.proposed: 改用“”或去掉引号
issues.rationale: “人”“账”不是原文引语，改用“”。

issues.problem: 中文已标“作者推断”“（作者解释）”，英文“It swaps one question for another…”等推断没有任何解释标签。
issues.proposed: 英文加“One reading is that…”或“The author infers that…”
issues.rationale: 英文推断句前加 The author infers that，与中文的“作者推断”和（作者解释）对应。

issues.problem: “吴起离鲁入魏”/“left Lu for Wei”在证据包中没有对应记载。证据直接从文侯问李克开始。
issues.proposed: 改为“后来，魏文侯问李克……”，不写离鲁入魏的过程
issues.rationale: 删去证据没有记载的“离鲁入魏”，改为“后来，魏文侯问李克……”。

issues.problem: “文侯用他为将”/“The marquis gave him command”没有证据。证据只记文侯以他为西河守。
issues.proposed: 删去该句，或改为“文侯后来以他为西河守”并移至story.2
issues.rationale: 删去“文侯用他为将”；带兵细节改以原文“起之為將”起句，任西河守的内容仍留在 story.2。

issues.problem: 英文李克答语加了引号，但实为译文，读者看不出是译述，可能误以为原话。

evidence.quote: 起貪而好色，然用兵司馬穰苴不能過也

issues.proposed: 引语前加“in the Records' words (here translated)”或改为间接引语
issues.rationale: 英文李克答语去掉引号，改为标明 rendered here in translation 的间接引语；同时删去证据未载的头衔 minister。

issues.problem: 本段为record，末句“这是本文里最刺眼的一笔：得士心的方式和它的代价……”是作者评断，中英都没有标注为解释。
issues.proposed: 加“作者认为”/“In the author's reading”
issues.rationale: 末句评断前加“作者认为”/In the author's reading。

issues.problem: 英文卒母的话用引号直接呈现，实为译文，没有标明是译述。

evidence.quote: 妾不知其死所矣。是以哭之

issues.proposed: 标明为译文，或改为间接引语
issues.rationale: 英文卒母之言去掉引号，改为标明译述的间接引语。

issues.problem: 吴起的答语以“由此觀之”开头，说明前面另有一段论证（不在证据包内，相关E9已被剔除）。正文把它写成武侯感叹后的直接回答，截断了语境。经核对，正文没有使用已剔除的E9内容。
issues.proposed: 写作“吴起的回答结尾说：「……由此觀之，在德不在險……」”，标明为节引
issues.rationale: 中文注明吴起的回答“此处只节引其结尾”；英文同步写 Of Wu Qi's reply only its conclusion is given here，不再写成直接回答。

issues.problem: 英文“Your Majesty”用于魏侯，称谓不当。原文为“君”。
issues.proposed: 改为“my lord”
issues.rationale: 英文 Your Majesty 改为 my lord，对应原文“君”。

issues.problem: 英文中武侯与吴起的话、“Well said”都是译文，却以引号直接呈现，没有标明是译述。

evidence.quote: 美哉乎山河之固，此魏國之寶也

issues.proposed: 标明为译文
issues.rationale: 英文武侯感叹、吴起答语和“善”都去掉引号，标明是译述（in paraphrase / in translation）。

issues.problem: 正文只列出两项论功（将三军、守西河），却接着写“这三件事”/“all three”。第三项不在证据包中，读者无法对应。
issues.proposed: 注明“（原文共论三事，此处录其二）”
issues.rationale: 中文加注“（原文共论三事，此处录其二。）”，英文同步加注。

issues.problem: 英文对话用引号直接呈现，实为译文，没有标明是译述。
issues.proposed: 标明为译文
issues.rationale: 英文对话去掉引号，标明 In translation and paraphrase，改为间接引语。

issues.problem: 英文田文、吴起的对话用引号直接呈现，实为译文，没有标明是译述。
issues.proposed: 标明为译文
issues.rationale: 英文田文、吴起的对话去掉引号，改为标明译述的间接引语。

issues.problem: 英文“a man called Gongsun Shu”中的名字“Gongsun Shu”证据中没有，原文只作“公叔”。

evidence.quote: 公叔為相，尚魏公主，而害吳起

issues.proposed: 改为“Gongshu (Lord Shu)”，不补写全名
issues.rationale: 英文删去证据没有的全名 Gongsun Shu，改为 Gongshu (Lord Shu)。

issues.problem: 原文“害吳起”指加害、与之为敌。英文“he feared Wu Qi”意思不符；中文“忌害”多出“忌”的动机成分。
issues.proposed: 中文改“想加害吴起”，英文改“was hostile to Wu Qi / sought to harm him”
issues.rationale: 中文“忌害”改为“想加害”，英文 feared 改为 sought to harm，去掉证据外的动机成分。

issues.problem: 英文中仆人与进言的话用引号直接呈现，实为译文，没有标明是译述。
issues.proposed: 标明为译文
issues.rationale: 英文仆人之言和试探之辞去掉引号，标明是译述。

issues.problem: 原文只写“廢公族疏遠者”，没有说明废除的是何种待遇。中文“待遇”和英文“stipends”是证据外的具体化。
issues.proposed: 改为“废黜与王室疏远的公族”/“removed distant members of the royal clan”
issues.rationale: 中文“废除疏远王族的待遇”改为“罢废与王室疏远的公族”，英文 abolished the stipends 改为 removed distant members of the royal clan，删去证据外的“待遇/stipends”。

issues.problem: 英文“could not bring himself to”“the restraint he had shown all his life”超出了中文的“平日的自持”，写成人物的内心和终身品性，而且与证据记载的“猜忍”、杀三十余人相冲突。
issues.proposed: 英文改为“declined the match… would not fit the self-image the servant attributed to him”，删去“all his life”
issues.rationale: 英文删去 could not bring himself to 和 the restraint he had shown all his life，改为 declined the match，并说明这与仆人所归于他的重名性情不合。中文“平日的自持”同步改为“仆人所描述的那种自惜名声的性情”，“照自己的性子行事”改为“正如仆人所料”，避免与“猜忍”的记载冲突。

issues.problem: 英文仆人评语用引号，实为译文，没有标明是译述。

evidence.quote: 吳起為人節廉而自喜名也

issues.proposed: 标明为译文
issues.rationale: 英文仆人评语去掉引号，标明 in translation。

issues.problem: 「无留心」放在「」内，但证据原文是“無留心”，不是逐字片段。
issues.proposed: 改为「無留心」或用“”
issues.rationale: 「无留心」不是逐字片段，改用“无留心”。

issues.problem: 英文“Marquis Wu grew suspicious…”“feared being punished and left”加了引号，实为译文，没有标明是译述。
issues.proposed: 标明为译文
issues.rationale: 英文两处引文去掉引号，标明为译述。另把 with results 改为 another chance to prove himself，与中文“下一次自证的机会”一致。

issues.problem: 「在德不在险」与证据原文“在德不在險”不一致，不是逐字片段。
issues.proposed: 改为「在德不在險」
issues.rationale: 「在德不在险」改为原文逐字的「在德不在險」。

issues.problem: 英文司马迁评语用引号，实为译文，没有标明是译述。
issues.proposed: 标明为译文
issues.rationale: 英文司马迁评语去掉引号，标明 rendered here in translation。

issues.problem: 英文“abolition of stipends for distant branches”把原文没有的“stipends”写成“能确认”的内容。
issues.proposed: 改为“the removal of distant members of the royal clan”
issues.rationale: 英文改为 the removal of distant members of the royal clan，删去 stipends；中文同步去掉正文中的证据编号。

issues.problem: 「一种解释是」「作者推断」用了「」，但它们是本文自己的措辞，不是证据中的逐字片段。
issues.proposed: 改用“”
issues.rationale: “一种解释是”“作者推断”是本文措辞，改用“”。英文原文不变，按同步规则一并给出。

issues.problem: 「摔门离开卫国」原文（SJ0651-E3）只作「東出衛郭門」，即从卫国都城东门出走，没有摔门这一动作
issues.audit_rationale: 原文只有“東出衛郭門”，没有摔门这一动作。
issues.rationale: 与 F8 同一处，已改为“从卫国郭门向东出走”，中英同步。

issues.problem: 「鲁君起疑，辞退了吴起」中的“辞退”在证据包中无对应记载（E1–E3 只记鲁疑之、鲁卒以为将及进谗内容，无罢免/谢吴起之文）
issues.audit_rationale: E1–E3没有鲁君罢免、辞退吴起的记载。
issues.rationale: 与 F9 同一处，已删去“辞退”，改为原文未记鲁君处置。

issues.problem: [unsupported_claims] 鲁君起疑，辞退了吴起（证据包无辞退/罢免记载）
issues.rationale: 与M2是同一问题。

issues.problem: [unsupported_claims] 摔门离开卫国（原文仅“東出衛郭門”）
issues.rationale: 与M1是同一问题。

issues.problem: [unsupported_claims] 文侯用他为将（证据包无“以为将”之文）
issues.audit_rationale: 证据只记以为西河守，没有“以为将”。
issues.rationale: 与 F14 同一处，story.0 已删去“文侯用他为将”。

issues.problem: [unsupported_claims] 吴起在魏国……位置稳固（无据）
issues.rationale: 与 F2 同一处，hook.0 已删去“位置稳固”。

issues.problem: [unsupported_claims] 就把公主请来，让她发怒（原文作“即令公主怒而輕君”，无“请来公主”）
issues.rationale: 现稿story.5作“令公主发怒、当面轻慢魏相”，没有“把公主请来”，与原文相符。

issues.problem: [invented_inner_life] 他可能判断解释已经无用，也可能担心解释本身会被当成「无留心」的又一件证据。
issues.rationale: 现稿已用“作者推断”“可能”标为推测，并说明原文只写他惧罪而去，没有当作事实写。

issues.problem: [invented_inner_life] 作者提出的替代选择是：当场把这场会面的经过讲给武侯，或者暂缓决定、等待下一次自证的机会（原文未写吴起考虑过这些选项，虽已声明）
issues.rationale: 现稿已标为“作者提出的替代选择”，并明说“原文没有写他考虑过这些选项”，属于标注清楚的反事实。

issues.problem: [invented_inner_life] 被试探者很难把「拒绝」说成一件大事去解释（泛化推断，非史料）
issues.rationale: 现稿以“一种解释是”和“（作者解释）”标明这是解释，讨论对象是计策设计本身，没有冒充史料。（英文缺标签的问题另列F5。）

issues.problem: [quote_mismatches] 「即令公主怒而輕君」被译作“就把公主请来，让她发怒，当面轻慢您”，增出原文没有的“把公主请来”
issues.rationale: 同M7，现稿中英文都没有“把公主请来”。

issues.problem: [quote_mismatches] 「往年吳公吮其父，其父戰不旋踵，遂死於敵」正文译“脚跟不转、向前战死在敌阵”，引语表译“作战不退，死在敌阵”，同一原句两处译法不一致
issues.rationale: 现稿没有引语表，只在story.1出现一种译法，不存在两处译法不一致。

evidence.quote: 其父戰不旋踵，遂死於敵

issues.problem: [quote_mismatches] 「起貪而好色」译作“吴起贪财又好色”，“财”字为增出的解释性成分
issues.rationale: 现稿中文逐字引原文，英文作“greedy”，没有“贪财”一类增译。

issues.problem: 段末“原文接着写，吴起自知不如田文 / The source adds that Wu Qi knew himself the lesser of the two”出自 E17，但该段证据只列了 E15、E16。这句陈述在所列证据中没有出处。
issues.proposed: 把 SJ0651-E17 加入 sections.story.4 的证据列表。
issues.rationale: 段末“吴起自知不如田文”出自 E17，现已把 SJ0651-E17 加入 sections.story.4 的证据列表。正文不变。

issues.problem: 英文把“公叔”加注为“(Lord Shu)”。证据只写“公叔”，没有支持把它拆解为“叔”这位领主的释义。这一注释有误导性，中文也没有对应内容，中英不一致。

evidence.quote: 田文既死，公叔為相，尚魏公主，而害吳起。

issues.proposed: 删去“(Lord Shu)”，只保留“Gongshu”。
issues.rationale: 证据只写“公叔”，不支持“Lord Shu”这一释义，因此删去英文中的“(Lord Shu)”，只保留 Gongshu。中文原本无此注，按同步规则一并给出未改动的中文全文。

issues.problem: 中文正文末尾夹带了内部证据编号“（SJ0651-E20）”，英文没有。这是编辑标记残留，中英不一致。

edits.before: After the victory, a courtier described him to the ruler of Lu like this: a suspicious, ruthless man. In his youth his family was worth a fortune; he went off seeking office, failed, and spent his fortune trying, until his neighbors laughed at him. He then killed more than thirty of those who had mocked him and walked out through the eastern gate of Wei's capital. Parting from his mother, he bit his arm and swore he would not return until he held the highest office. She died, and he never went back, whereupon Zengzi broke with him. The speech then turned to the arithmetic: Lu is a small state, and once it carries the name of a victory, the other lords will begin to plot against it. Lu and Wei are brother states; to employ Wu Qi is to slight Wei. The ruler of Lu grew suspicious and dismissed him.
edits.after: After the victory, a courtier described him to the ruler of Lu like this: a suspicious, ruthless man. In his youth his family was worth a fortune; he went off seeking office, failed, and ran through the family fortune, until his neighbors laughed at him. He then killed more than thirty of those who had mocked him and went out eastward through the outer gate of Wey's city wall. Parting from his mother, he bit his arm and swore he would not return to Wey until he became a high minister or chancellor. She died, and he never went back, whereupon Zengzi broke with him. The speech then turned to the arithmetic: Lu is a small state, and once it carries the name of a victory, the other lords will begin to plot against Lu. Lu and Wey are brother states; to employ Wu Qi is to abandon Wey. The text relied on here ends with this speech and records nothing of how the ruler of Lu responded.

edits.before: Wu Qi left Lu for Wei. Marquis Wen of Wei asked the minister Li Ke what sort of man Wu Qi was. Li Ke answered: "Wu Qi is greedy and fond of women, but when it comes to command, even Sima Rangju could not surpass him." The marquis gave him command. In the field Wu Qi wore the same clothes and ate the same food as the lowest of his soldiers. He slept without a mat, rode neither horse nor cart on the march, wrapped and carried his own share of grain, and shared the men's toil and hardship.
edits.after: Later, Marquis Wen of Wei asked Li Ke what sort of man Wu Qi was. Li Ke replied — rendered here in translation — that Wu Qi was greedy and fond of women, but that in commanding troops even Sima Rangju could not surpass him. As a general, Wu Qi wore the same clothes and ate the same food as the lowest of his soldiers. He slept without a mat, rode neither horse nor cart on the march, wrapped and carried his own share of grain, and shared the men's toil and hardship.

edits.before: One soldier developed a carbuncle, and Wu Qi sucked the poison from it himself. The soldier's mother heard of this and wept. Someone asked her: the general tended to your own son — why do you cry? "It is not that," she said. "Years ago Lord Wu did the same for the boy's father. His father went into battle without turning on his heels and died in the enemy's ranks. Now Lord Wu has done it again for my son, and I do not know where this child will meet his death. That is why I weep." It is the most jarring stroke in the whole story: the way he won his men's hearts, and what that cost, are written in the same tears.
edits.after: One soldier developed a carbuncle, and Wu Qi sucked the poison from it himself. The soldier's mother heard of this and wept. Someone asked her why she wept, when the general himself had tended her son's carbuncle. Her answer, given here in translation and paraphrase: it was not as they thought. Years ago Lord Wu had done the same for the boy's father, who then went into battle without turning on his heels and died at the enemy's hands. Now Lord Wu had done it again for her son, and she did not know where this child would meet his death. That was why she wept. In the author's reading, it is the most jarring stroke in the whole story: the way he won his men's hearts, and what that cost, are written in the same tears.

edits.before: Marquis Wen judged him skilled in war, honest and fair, and able to win the hearts of his men, and made him governor of Xihe to hold off Qin and Han. Once Marquis Wu was drifting down the West River; in midstream he turned and sighed, "How magnificent — these mountains and rivers, so secure: a treasure of the state of Wei!" Wu Qi answered: "From this it can be seen that safety lies in virtue, not in natural defenses. If Your Majesty does not cultivate virtue, everyone in this boat will become an enemy state." Marquis Wu said, "Well said."
edits.after: Marquis Wen judged him skilled in war, honest and fair, and able to win the hearts of his men, and made him governor of Xihe to hold off Qin and Han. Of Wu Qi's reply only its conclusion is given here, in translation: from this it can be seen that safety lies in virtue, not in natural defenses; if my lord does not cultivate virtue, everyone in this boat will become an enemy state. Marquis Wu approved, calling it well said.

edits.before: 后来魏国置相，相田文，吴起不悦，提出与田文论功。（SJ0651-E11）他问：统率三军，使士卒乐死、敌国不敢谋，你比我如何？田文答「不如子」。（SJ0651-E12）又问：守住西河，秦兵不敢东向，韩赵宾从，你比我如何？田文仍答「不如子」。（SJ0651-E13）吴起说，这三件事你都在我之下，位子却在我之上，为什么？（SJ0651-E14）

edits.before: In time Wei appointed a chancellor, and the office went to Tian Wen. Wu Qi was displeased and challenged him to compare their merits. "Commanding the three armies, making the soldiers glad to die, so that no enemy state dares to plot against us — how do you compare with me?" Tian Wen said, "I am not your equal." "Holding Xihe, so that the armies of Qin dare not turn eastward and Han and Zhao come as obedient followers — how do you compare with me?" "I am not your equal." Wu Qi pressed the point: "In all three of these you fall below me, yet your rank stands above mine. Why?"
edits.after: In time Wei appointed a chancellor, and the office went to Tian Wen. Wu Qi was displeased and challenged him to compare their merits. In translation and paraphrase, the exchange runs as follows. Wu Qi asked how Tian Wen compared with him in commanding the three armies, making the soldiers glad to die, so that no enemy state dared to plot; Tian Wen said he was not his equal. Wu Qi asked how Tian Wen compared with him in holding Xihe, so that the armies of Qin dared not turn eastward and Han and Zhao came as obedient followers; again Tian Wen said he was not his equal. (The original weighs three matters; two are given here.) Wu Qi pressed the point: in all three of these Tian Wen fell below him, yet his rank stood above Wu Qi's — why?

edits.before: 田文答：「主少國疑，大臣未附，百姓不信，方是之時，屬之於子乎？屬之於我乎？」（SJ0651-E15）吴起默然良久，说：「屬之子矣。」田文说，这正是我位居你之上的原因。（SJ0651-E16）原文接着写，吴起自知不如田文。
edits.after: 田文答：「主少國疑，大臣未附，百姓不信，方是之時，屬之於子乎？屬之於我乎？」吴起默然良久，说：「屬之子矣。」田文说，这正是我位居你之上的原因。原文接着写，吴起自知不如田文。

edits.before: Tian Wen answered: "Our ruler is young and the state uncertain, the great ministers have not attached themselves to him, and the people do not trust him. At such a moment, should the state be entrusted to you, or to me?" Wu Qi fell silent for a long time. "It should be entrusted to you," he said. Tian Wen replied, "That is precisely why I sit above you." The source adds that Wu Qi knew himself the lesser of the two.
edits.after: Tian Wen answered — rendered here in translation — that the ruler was young and the state uncertain, the great ministers had not attached themselves to him, and the people did not trust him; at such a moment, should the state be entrusted to Wu Qi, or to Tian Wen? Wu Qi fell silent for a long time, then said it should be entrusted to Tian Wen. Tian Wen replied that this was precisely why he sat above Wu Qi. The source adds that Wu Qi knew himself the lesser of the two.

edits.before: 田文死后，公叔为相，娶魏公主，忌害吴起。公叔的仆人说了一句很轻的话：「起易去也。」（SJ0651-E17）计策分两步。第一步是进言：吴起是贤人，而魏国小，又与强秦接壤，恐怕他没有长留之心；不妨以公主的婚事试探他——「起有留心則必受之。無留心則必辭矣。以此卜之。」（SJ0651-E18）第二步是安排：召吴起一同回家，令公主发怒、当面轻慢魏相。（SJ0651-E19）
edits.after: 田文死后，公叔为相，娶魏公主，想加害吴起。公叔的仆人说了一句很轻的话：「起易去也。」计策分两步。第一步是进言：吴起是贤人，而魏国小，又与强秦接壤，恐怕他没有长留之心；不妨以公主的婚事试探他——「起有留心則必受之。無留心則必辭矣。以此卜之。」第二步是安排：召吴起一同回家，令公主发怒、当面轻慢魏相。

edits.before: After Tian Wen died, a man called Gongsun Shu became chancellor; he had married a Wei princess, and he feared Wu Qi. His servant said something very light: "Wu Qi is easy to remove." The scheme ran in two steps. First, the whisper to the marquis: Wu Qi is a man of talent, but Wei is a small state and borders mighty Qin; I fear he has no thought of staying. Test him with the offer of a princess — "If Wu Qi means to stay, he will certainly accept; if he has no such intention, he will certainly decline. Use this to gauge him." Second, the arrangement: invite Wu Qi home with the chancellor, and have the princess lose her temper and slight the chancellor in front of him.
edits.after: After Tian Wen died, Gongshu (Lord Shu) became chancellor; he had married a Wei princess, and he sought to harm Wu Qi. His servant said something very light — in translation, that Wu Qi was easy to remove. The scheme ran in two steps. First, a word to the marquis: Wu Qi is a man of talent, but Wei is a small state and borders mighty Qin; I fear he has no thought of staying.
